question: With the same source bit pattern and channel, how does 35 to 70 ps source rise time change the RX eye and finite-pattern decisions?
hypothesis: Slower source edges may reduce the vertical sampling margin through intersymbol interference. No recipe search or pass/fail target tuning.
changed_parameter: rise_ps only: first-order source 10-90% rise time, 35 to 70 ps
primary_metrics: Worst signed threshold margin at 0.5 UI and 0.5 V [V]

definitions.opening: min(v at bit=1) - max(v at bit=0)
definitions.signed_margin: For bit 1: v - threshold; for bit 0: threshold - v; report minimum over retained pattern
definitions.mismatch: Sample threshold decisions compared with the retained source bits; not statistical BER

numerical_conventions.spatial_mesh: None: two lossless transmission-line delay queues
numerical_conventions.sampling: Fixed 64 samples/UI; delays rounded to nearest sample
numerical_conventions.alignment: Nominal launch clock plus quantized RX flight time; no CDR or strobe optimization
